To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have established a high confidence, manually-validated human blood plasma protein list using two high-end mass spectrometry instruments and a statistical score that is based on two stages of tandem mass spectroscopy.

a combination of LTQ Orbitrap and LTQ FT MS3, with a high mass accuracy of 2.5 and 5ppm for the LTQ FT and the LTQ Orbitrap, respectively, allows the identification of peptides with a very high confidence, and that this high confidence can be achieved for a large number of plasma proteins.
we have established a high confidence reference set of 697 proteins in human blood plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high confidence reference set of blood plasma proteins.
the establishment of a high confidence reference set of human plasma proteins that will facilitate the discovery of potential novel biomarkers for future clinical diagnostics.
the identification and characterization of the human plasma protein complement, and our results will facilitate the identification of novel disease biomarkers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have established a high confidence, manually verified set of plasma proteins that can be used to facilitate the identification of biomarkers for various diseases.
our list of 697 plasma protein is a high confidence list of plasma proteins, with a very low false peptide identification error rate.

the plasma proteome is a dynamic, complex and challenging proteome, and it is only with high end instrumentation and a rigorous validation procedure that one can obtain a high confidence protein list.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established an ultra high confidence set of plasma proteins that will be useful for future biomarker research.
the plasma proteome is very complex, and that the use of high end mass spectrometry instruments is essential to obtain an accurate list of plasma proteins.

the use of high accuracy MS3 peptide identification searching combined with high mass accuracy parent ion measurements allows the identification of plasma proteins with an unprecedented level of confidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma proteome is much more tractable than previously thought and that the use of MS3 and very high mass accuracy MS can be used to identify plasma proteins at very high confidence.
the use of high mass accuracy MS instruments combined with rigorous validation can result in a high confidence list of blood plasma proteins.

the use of high end instrumentation and a stringent statistical treatment can yield an ultra high confidence plasma protein reference list that can serve as a benchmark for future plasma proteomics studies.
